metadata.title: Seattle mayor says police arrested a 15-year-old after a festival shooting that killed 3 near the Space Needle

sources.news_title: Teen arrested after mass shooting at market
sources.text:
Police confirmed Monday a 15-year-old has been detained in connection with Sunday’s shooting at the Seattle Center.
Two men, aged 18 and 44, and a woman, aged 56, were killed and several others — including a toddler — were wounded.
Seattle police are working to identify a second suspect in the shooting at a popular food festival at the foot of the city’s iconic Space Needle.
Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today
Authorities believe two people were shooting at each other, according to Seattle Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis, who said there is no ongoing threat to the public.
There were at least seven victims caught in the crossfire, possibly eight, Davis said in a Monday news conference. When asked whether the second suspect could be one of the victims killed, Davis said, “it is possible but we do not know that that is the case until we do the investigation”.
Police are asking for those with information about the shooting to come forward.
The deadly Sunday-evening shooting at the Bite of Seattle, a free event that draws hundreds of thousands of guests each year, sent attendees running for their lives.
A large group was seen knocking down a fence to escape after a volley of gunfire, the latest gruesome entry in the ever-expanding log of Americans victimised by gun violence while doing everyday activities.
Authorities responded to reports of shots fired just after 6pm at the Seattle Center.
“There were about six or seven, multiple gunshots,” Justice Beitzel, who was eating with friends as a concert played nearby, told CNN’s Ben Hunte.
“All of a sudden, I just saw people running towards us.”
Two people were declared dead at the scene. Another victim died after being taken to a local hospital, Davis said late Sunday.
In emergency dispatch audio obtained by CNN, one person was heard requesting a “small child tourniquet” for a victim at the scene.
A 2-year-old boy was taken to Harborview Medical Center, the fire department said Sunday. By Monday morning, the toddler remained at the hospital in “satisfactory condition,” according to Susan Gregg, the hospital’s media relations director.
A few other victims were seen at local hospitals, including a 23-year-old man and 39-year-old woman who have since been discharged from Harborview, and a 27-year-old man who was released from nearby UW Medical Center – Montlake, Gregg added.
Police recovered two weapons and said two people were believed to be shooting at each other. Davis described the suspect in custody as a young person.
What prompted the shooting isn’t known. Authorities urged people who witnessed the shooting to come forward with any information that could be helpful for the investigation.
The shooting is one of at least 271 mass shootings in the US this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as one in which four or more victims are shot.
The Seattle Center spans a 74-acre campus and is home to the Space Needle and the city’s largest arena, drawing more than 12 million visitors each year.
And hundreds of thousands of those visitors bring their appetites to the center for the annual Bite of Seattle Festival, which hosts hundreds of local vendors offering creative foods and live entertainment across three days.
Crowds of people walked through the aisles of outdoor vendors Sunday, passing plates of poke, bowls of noodles and freshly grilled seafood. Social media users gleefully documented their cheese pulls and noodle swirls in videos shared online.
As shots were fired, the jovial mood turned to panic. Festival-goers rushed to flee the danger.
A livestream from food vendor Hawaiian Honey Cones captured a man speaking to the camera as at least four gunshots rang out in the background.
People ducked and ran from the scene as a large group of attendees knocked down a fence on their way out of the area.
In the aftermath of the chaos, witnesses shared varying accounts of what they saw and heard.
Two witnesses told CNN affiliate KOMO they heard seven to eight gunshots, as people ran in all directions. Another attendee said he was near a stage where a band was performing, when he heard at least two dozen shots.
Another man said some people didn’t react right away, thinking, “Oh it must be fireworks or something.”
But after more shots were heard, he saw people “storming through the area” trying to get out.
Some people appeared to take shelter in the gift shop of the Space Needle at the Seattle Center, video shared with CNN showed.
Police, emergency responders and officers from several agencies, including the FBI, were at the scene afterward, video showed.
A Washington state SWAT team was also on its way to assist at the request of Seattle police, Gov. Bob Ferguson said.
CNN has reached out to Seattle police and city officials, as well as the Seattle Center, the FBI, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson called the shooting “an act of horrific violence” and said the community “is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire.”
“In the days ahead, we will establish what happened and be transparent with the public about what we have learned,” Wilson wrote.
“Tonight, our attention belongs to the people whose lives were taken, those fighting to recover, and the families beside them.”

sources.news_title: Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson Faces Backlash After Mass Shooting For Deactivating CCTV Cameras › American Greatness
sources.text:
In the wake of a mass shooting in Seattle Sunday, the city’s Socialist Mayor Katie Wilson is facing scrutiny for deactivating surveillance cameras in parts of the city to protect criminals and illegal aliens.
A shootout between two thugs at Seattle’s Bite of Seattle food festival Sunday evening left three people dead and four others injured, including a toddler.
Seattle Police and SWAT teams responded within seconds, performing emergency aid at the scene and launching a search for suspects. Police reportedly recovered two guns at the scene.
Police identified the deceased victims as a 19-year-old man, 44-year-old man, and 56-year-old woman.
A two-year-old boy, 23-year-old man, 39-year-old woman, and a 40-year-old woman received minor injuries, with three in stable condition at an area hospital, and one declining hospital transport.
Only one suspect was taken into custody—a 15-year-old black male who is being held in a juvenile detention facility.
The teen is being held for investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault, Mayor Wilson announced in a news conference Monday.
The other suspect remains at large, and Seattle Police are asking for tips from the public to find him.
The shooting occurred at around 6 p.m. during the annual three-day festival at the Seattle Center featuring hundreds of food vendors, live music, and a large crowd.
Investigators told reporters Sunday that no surveillance cameras were present at the site to help track the suspect, possibly due to Wilson’s fierce opposition to the crime-fighting tools.
The far-left mayor has vocally opposed putting CCTV cameras in public spaces, saying they “put refugees at risk.”
“Turning on more cameras won’t magically make our neighborhoods safer, but it will certainly make our neighborhoods more vulnerable,” she said in 2025 after the Seattle City Council approved the expansion of the Real Time Crime Center, a CCTV pilot program.
Wilson has ordered an audit reviewing policies and practices governing all cameras connected to the program, including how the data is stored and used, KOMO News reported. No new police CCTV cameras may be activated while the city awaits the results of the audit.
The mayor said in an online post that cameras are still allowed to operate in the Chinatown-International District, and along Aurora Avenue North.
She had previously declined to turn newly installed Stadium District cameras on for the FIFA World Cup, but relented in June, announcing that the cameras could be activated during the World Cup, “because of its high profile and the unique circumstance surrounding the event.”
On July 7, the day after the FIFA World Cup concluded, Wilson immediately had the Stadium-District surveillance cameras deactivated. The Seattle Event Center is located about seven miles to North of the Stadium district.
Downtown Seattle Association President and CEO Jon Scholes pushed back on Wilson’s decision, arguing the cameras should stay on to protect the local community.
“Deactivating Seattle’s safety cameras makes zero sense,” Scholes said in a statement to KIRO Newsradio. “Massive crowds with international visitors may have left, but the community remains, and their safety should be supported by the best available resources. Cameras are helping keep our buses, light rail trains, airports, ports and roads safe. They’re a critical tool law enforcement utilizes to solve crimes, providing crucial evidence, while having important privacy code built into their use to protect the public. Turning off the cameras is blindfolding law enforcement and makes it harder to solve crimes.”
Federal investigators say surveillance cameras are key to solving crimes, providing the technical forensic analysis needed to bring the cases to a quick close.
Police are now having to rely on phone camera footage from witnesses at the event to find the second suspect.

sources.news_title: Seattle police arrest 15-year-old suspect over food festival shooting that killed three
sources.text:
Police now say there were at least three suspects involved in a food festival shooting near Seattle’s Space Needle over the weekend, and that one of them was among those killed in the violence.
In a document filed in juvenile court in Seattle, where a 15-year-old arrested in the case was making an initial appearance Monday, police said they believe there were at least three shooters: the 15-year-old; an acquaintance who died at the scene; and “at least one other unknown suspect.”
“Based on the evidence at the scene, investigators believe” the 15-year-old “and one of the deceased engaged in a gunfight with at least one other unknown suspect,” the document said.
The teen was being held in juvenile detention for investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault ahead of the afternoon court appearance, Mayor Katie Wilson said at a news conference.
Authorities said earlier Monday they are still looking for an additional suspect, but could not rule out whether that individual was among those killed.
“We are trying to identify who that person is,” said Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes.
Investigators had said they believed the two suspects were shooting at each other. Police said late Sunday night it was not clear whether any of the victims had been involved in the confrontation between the two shooters.
Two people died at the scene and a third died at a hospital. They were described as two men, ages 19 and 44, and a woman, 56.
Police search for second suspect after deadly Seattle food festival shooting
The four wounded included a 2-year-old boy, who was in satisfactory condition Monday. The others – two men, ages 23 and 27, and a woman, 39 – were discharged, a hospital spokesperson said.
Vendors were allowed to return to the sprawling campus Monday morning to clean up and collect their equipment and merchandise. Skewered squid on grills, roasted ducks in ovens and plates full of food were among the items left behind as people fled the gunfire.
Near the spot of the shooting, a stain of what appeared to be blood was still visible in the morning. A candlelight vigil was planned Monday night at the centre’s International Fountain.
The gunfire erupted around 6 p.m. Sunday in the waning hours of the Bite of Seattle. The annual three-day festival draws hundreds of food and retail vendors and performers to Seattle Center, a sprawling park and event space in the shadow of the Space Needle. Many attendees rushed into campus buildings or ran from the park at the sound of the shots.
Dozens of officers were providing security at the event and some saw one of the suspects firing, authorities said. A large number of police and emergency crews responded and began evacuating the area. Police then searched an IMAX theatre on the grounds where they initially believed a second shooter had fled.
Adam Lombardo, who had a Burmese food stand at the festival with his spouse, described the panic of fleeing people as a “stampede.” As he gathered his equipment Monday, he described how police escorted them into the crime scene to turn off their ovens and stoves.
“It’s really sad because you think that three innocent people aren’t getting up with their families,” he said. “They just came to enjoy a food festival with people, with friends, with new friends, and they lost their lives in just what sounds like meaningless bloodshed.”
Festival attendee Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just gotten food from a crepe vendor when gunfire broke out nearby. In the scramble to find safety, she and others ran into the nearby Seattle Children’s Museum.
“We were about to start eating, then heard someone yell something, then we saw people start to run,” Hunter said. “So we took off running, too.”
Roberto Ramirez, a vendor at the event, said he heard what sounded like firecrackers before people began yelling “shooter” and frantically running.
“Suddenly everything was empty,” he said. “People were freaked out.”
After the initial panic, new guests continued to arrive, unaware of what had happened. Police told them to leave, he said.
Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and turned to see a rush of people fleeing.
“People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling,” Wakonabo said, adding that was when he heard gunshots.
“Once I heard a ‘pop, pop, pop,’ that’s when I knew it was a shooter,” he said.
After he escorted his girlfriend to safety, he returned to the scene to take photos and saw multiple victims on the ground, Wakonabo said.
The festival started in 1982 and draws 350,000 attendees, according to its website.

sources.news_title: Police arrest 15-year-old after Seattle festival shooting that killed 3
SPD Says 15-year-old in Custody After Gunfight at Seattle Center Kills Three
sources.text:
Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson and Seattle Police Department Chief Shon Barnes said during a Monday morning press conference that yesterday’s deadly shooting at Seattle Center was the result of two people shooting at each other and hitting bystanders.
Wilson said a 15-year-old is being held at King County’s youth jail for a firearm offense and first-degree assault, and will make a first appearance in court today at 1:30 p.m.
Chief Barnes said police are still searching for a second shooter, but have not yet identified who that person is. Barnes said a SWAT team searched the Seattle Center yesterday searching for a second shooter, but found no one.
Barnes said witnesses should report what they saw to SPD’s tipline, and Mayor Wilson said investigators are checking footage from Seattle Center security cameras.
As for a motive, Barnes said he didn’t “know if it’s gang activity, but certainly group activity.”
Barnes said while it is possible one of the victims of the shooting is the second shooter, there has been no confirmation of that, and the investigation is ongoing. Authorities have yet to publicly identify any of the victims.
Seattle Fire Department Chief Harold Scoggins says two men, aged 19 and 44, died on the scene, and a 56-year-old woman died of her injuries at Harborview Medical Center.
Two women, aged 40 and 39, as well as a 23-year-old man were transported to Harborview and have since been discharged. A two-year-old boy remains in Harborview in “satisfactory” condition.
A 27-year-old man also showed up to UW Medical Center’s Montlake campus last night with a gunshot wound, and was later discharged, though SPD is still investigating whether his injuries were related to the Seattle Center shooting.

sources.news_title: 15-year-old detained in connection to Bite of Seattle mass shooting that killed 3, hurt 4
sources.text:
Documents allege 3 people involved in 'gunfight' at Bite of Seattle that killed 3, hurt 4
SEATTLE (KOMO) — A mass shooting during the Bite of Seattle festival at Seattle Center on Sunday evening left three people dead and at least four others injured, including a 2-year-old boy, according to the Seattle police and fire departments.
In a Monday morning update, police said a 15-year-old suspect was detained and booked for first-degree assault and firearms violations. The mayor said no one has formally been arrested for investigation of homicide.
Court documents released Monday afternoon show there were allegedly three people involved in a "gunfight" that erupted in the middle of the food festival, and one of them died at the scene.
"Based on the evidence at the scene, investigators believe [the 15-year-old suspect] and one of the deceased engaged in a gunfight with at least one other unknown suspect."
The three victims who died in the shooting were identified as a 19-year-old man, a 44-year-old man, and a 56-year-old woman. It's currently unknown which of those three individuals was one of the alleged shooters.
And the third "unknown suspect" has yet to be identified.
In an 11 a.m. press conference Monday, city officials said that a 15-year-old suspect had been taken into custody for investigation of first-degree assault and firearms violations in connection with the shooting. Police had said they were working to identify a second suspect.
Investigators said early reports indicate that two suspects exchanged gunfire outside the Seattle Center Armory and bystanders were caught in the crossfire.
PHOTOS | Scene of mass shooting at Bite of Seattle
Police said they don't believe the public is in danger, and investigators are working to identify the other person involved in the shooting.
Mayor Katie Wilson confirmed that there are CCTV cameras at Seattle Center, and that law enforcement are currently pulling and reviewing the footage.
The three people who died were a 19-year-old man, a 44-year-old man, and a 56-year-old woman. Two of those victims died at the scene.
Four people, including the 2-year-old boy, were taken to Harborview Medical Center. One of those victims died at the hospital.
As of Sunday night, Harborview officials said three victims were in satisfactory condition: a 39-year-old woman, a 23-year-old man and the 2-year-old. Hospital officials said their injuries involved gunshot wounds to the leg, abdomen and arm.
On Monday morning, the man and the woman had been discharged from the hospital, and the toddler remained at Harborview, according to UW Medicine spokesperson Susan Gregg.
In addition, a 27-year-old man with a gunshot wound arrived at UW Medical Center - Montlake in satisfactory condition on Sunday. He has since been discharged.
Gregg said the hospital regularly prepares for incidents like this.
“It’s a busy time for Harborview, it’s the trauma center, it’s the summer. It’s very busy; this is what we’re meant to do. We’re always ready because we’re a level one trauma center, so if something like this happens, an unfortunate shooting, then we deliver and that’s what we did this evening,” Gregg said.
On Monday morning, a security guard at Seattle Center said the areas where the vendors were located were closed to the public while they packed up their stands. Some food vendors still had items on the grill after they were forced to flee amid the chaos.
A large police presence remained at the scene.
One of the questions being asked after Sunday's shooting is why it took police so long to hold a news conference.
The news conference with police, the mayor and several political leaders did not begin until just before 11 p.m., nearly five hours after the shots were fired.
RELATED | 3 killed, multiple injured, including toddler, in mass shooting at Bite of Seattle
A Seattle Police Department spokesperson said some dignitaries wanted to attend the news conference, but did not specify who they were.
Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal's Office released a statement regarding the delay.
"Congresswoman Jayapal learned about the incident shortly after it occurred and was on Zoom briefings from her home at 8 and 9 p.m. She was notified of the press conference at 10:10 p.m. and immediately proceeded to the site from her home in Seattle.”
Police said gunfire erupted just after 6 p.m. during the popular event. Video from a vendor captured frantic bystanders running away from the area just north of the Seattle Center Armory as officers ran toward the shots. Witnesses could be heard yelling and screaming as people fled, including some carrying children.
Mayor Katie Wilson called the shooting “an unbelievable tragedy.”
“I’m sorry that we’re having to gather here tonight under these tragic circumstances,” Wilson said.
Acting Seattle Police Chief Tyrone Davis said officers were already at the event and moved toward the gunfire.
“This is a tragedy. I’m really sorry that this happened. The Bite of Seattle is a very positive event. We haven’t had any issues in recent years. Thankfully, we had officers on scene who were brave, went toward those shots, and prevented more victims from being injured,” Davis said.
Seattle police confirmed one suspected shooter remained at large, while another suspect — described by police as a “young person” — was arrested. Officers took one person into custody and brought him to police headquarters to be interviewed.
According to Mayor Katie Wilson, the detained suspect is a 15-year-old boy.
The Youth Peace & Justice Foundation is offering a reward of up to $5,000 for information leading to the identification and arrest of any outstanding suspect(s) in the shooting.
A witness identified only as Andrew described hearing gunfire and then seeing people rush to escape.
“I heard a couple pops, but I didn’t think it was anything big until I saw people running. I saw families, kids, just everybody running out of the fair,” he said.
The King County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office said the suspect who was arrested would likely appear in court Monday morning, and more information would be available after that court appearance.
The event drew more than 300,000 people.
Anyone with information is asked to call the Seattle Police Department Tip Line at 206-233-5000.
Pacific Science Center is closed Monday, with all shows and general admission canceled. The Seattle Center Armory is also closed.
It has been more than a decade since there was a shooting at Seattle Center.
In May 2012, a man was injured after being shot in the leg at the Folklife Festival.
Court documents at the time said the shooter and another person were fighting when the shooter pulled out a revolver and fired four shots.
One of those shots hit a man who was walking nearby. He recovered in the hospital.
According to Seattle's crime dashboard, Sunday's three deaths were the second, third, and fourth homicides in the city this month.
Last month, the city celebrated its first homicide-free June in more than 50 years.
However, there have been 15 homicides in Seattle this year. The number is on pace for the fewest since 2020.
Last year set the decade's record low at 32.

sources.news_title: 15-year-old arrested after Seattle Center mass shooting leaves 3 dead, 4 wounded
sources.text:
A 15-year-old was taken into custody as police continue to search for a second suspect after three people were killed, and four others were wounded Sunday in a mass shooting at the Seattle Center, according to Mayor Katie Wilson and police.
"We believe this teenager opened fire in the crowd, but details are still under investigation," Wilson said.
No homicide charges have been filed against the teen, who was booked into juvenile detention on suspicion of firearms violations and first-degree assault, Wilson said. The juvenile was expected to make an initial court appearance Monday.
Seattle Police Department Chief Shon Barnes said investigators believe two individuals exchanged gunfire outside the Seattle Center Armory, leaving multiple bystanders caught in the crossfire.
MULTIPLE INJURED AFTER FLOATPLANE MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING, CATCHES FIRE OFF WASHINGTON COAST
Police believe the shooting stemmed from a conflict between two small groups who appear to be at odds with each other.
An active manhunt remains underway for the second suspected shooter. However, police acknowledged it is technically possible that one of the fatally shot victims was the second gunman, though that has not been confirmed.
Officials said a 19-year-old man and a 44-year-old man died at the scene despite life-saving efforts by first responders.
A 56-year-old woman was also transported to a local hospital in critical condition, where she later died.
Four other victims were injured, including a 2-year-old boy, a 23-year-old man, a 39-year-old woman and a 40-year-old woman. Officials said the toddler, who was initially transported to the hospital in stable condition, has since been upgraded to satisfactory condition. The remaining victims either suffered minor injuries or had already been discharged from the hospital.
Police are also investigating whether a 27-year-old man who self-transported to a hospital was an eighth victim. His involvement has not yet been confirmed.
Harborview Medical Center spokesperson Susan Gregg previously said the injuries to four patients involved an arm, abdomen and legs.
Wilson called the shooting "an act of horrific violence."
"Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire," Wilson said in a statement. "No one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event, gathering with friends, or experiencing their city."
The venue was hosting the Bite of Seattle food festival over the weekend.
"Our first responsibilities are supporting grieving families, caring for the injured, and providing clear and accurate information for the public," the mayor said.
Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson previously said he was receiving briefings and State Patrol SWAT officers responded to the scene to assist Seattle Police.
"My prayers are with the families of the victims, and the responders as they work to keep people safe," the governor said on X.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Seattle Police Department for additional information.
Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said she was "absolutely horrified" by the shooting.
"My heart goes out to the victims and their families, and all those impacted by this senseless violence."
"I am grateful to the officers and first responders who are at the scene and working to protect our community, as well as the frontline medical professionals who are treating survivors," she said on X. "Tonight, we grieve with our community in Seattle as well as those around the country affected by gun violence and mass shootings."
King County Executive Girmay Zahilay similarly said he was "horrified" by the violence.
"As someone who grew up in this community, I know what this event means to so many families, young people, and neighbors across our region," he said in a statement. "For years, the Bite has been one of Seattle's signature summer traditions. To see violence at a place that brings so many people together is heartbreaking and unacceptable."
Kayla Carris, 22, said she was sitting outside the Armory at the Bite of Seattle when people began to scream and run for cover inside the Seattle Center Armory.

"Everyone was just throwing stuff and running," Carris told The Seattle Times. "Like everyone."
Todd Behrends, 59, said he heard what appeared to be several rounds of shots.
People began running and jumping over each other to escape, Behrends told the outlet. One woman fell, and someone stepped on her leg.
Behrends said he saw a woman on the ground and a man on a stretcher as he ran toward an exit.

sources.news_title: Police arrested a 15-year-old after festival shooting that killed 3 in Seattle
sources.text:
A suspect arrested after a shootout that killed three people and left at least four others injured at a crowded food festival near Seattle's Space Needle over the weekend is 15 years old, the city's mayor said Monday.
The teen was being held in juvenile detention for investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault and was due to appear in court Monday afternoon, Mayor Katie Wilson said at a news conference.
Authorities said Monday they are still looking for a second suspect, but could not rule out whether the second suspect was among those killed.
"We are trying to identify who that person is," said Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes. Police did not have a description of the potential outstanding suspect.
IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Teen pleads guilty in deadly Georgia high school shooting
Investigators believe the two individuals were shooting at each other. Police said late Sunday night it was not clear whether any of the victims had been involved in the confrontation between the two shooters.
Two people died at the scene and a third died at a hospital. They were described as two men, ages 19 and 44, and a woman, 56.
The four wounded included a 2-year-old boy, who was in satisfactory condition Monday. The others — two men, ages 23 and 27, and a woman, 39 — were discharged, a hospital spokesperson said.
Vendors who had abandoned their food booths were cleaning up Monday. A candlelight vigil was planned Monday night at the center's International Fountain.
The gunfire erupted around 6 p.m. Sunday in the waning hours of the Bite of Seattle. The annual three-day festival draws hundreds of food and retail vendors and performers to Seattle Center, a sprawling park and event space in the shadow of the Space Needle. Many attendees rushed into campus buildings or ran from the park at the sound of the shots.
Dozens of officers were providing security at the event and some saw one of the suspects firing, authorities said. A large number of police and emergency crews responded and began evacuating the area. Police then searched an IMAX theater on the grounds where they initially believed a second shooter had fled.
Festival attendee Faith Adia Hunter said she and her friends had just gotten food from a crepe vendor when gunfire broke out.
"We were about to start eating, then heard someone yell something, then we saw people start to run," Hunter said. "So we took off running, too."
"We were right next to him when it started, so we took off running," Hunter added.
Hunter said that in the scramble to find safety, she and others ran into the nearby Seattle Children's Museum.
Roberto Ramirez, a vendor at the event, said he heard what sounded like firecrackers before people began yelling "shooter" and frantically running.
"Suddenly everything was empty," he said. "People were freaked out."
IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Texas gunman killed 1, wounded 10 after shooting at officer days earlier
After the initial panic, new guests continued to arrive, unaware of what had happened. Police told them to leave, he said.
Estan Wakonabo said he and his girlfriend were waiting in line for a photo booth when he was shoved from behind and turned to see a rush of people fleeing.
"People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling," Wakonabo said, adding that was when he heard gunshots.
"Once I heard a 'pop, pop, pop,' that's when I knew it was a shooter," he said.
After he escorted his girlfriend to safety, he returned to the scene to take photos and saw multiple victims on the ground, Wakonabo said.
The festival started in 1982 and draws 350,000 attendees, according to its website.

sources.news_title: Seattle Shooting Near Space Needle: What We Know So Far
sources.text:
Seattle Shooting Near Space Needle: What We Know So Far
A deadly shooting occurred near Seattle’s iconic Space Needle, drawing swift response from authorities. While details are still emerging, officials have confirmed fatalities and launched an investigation as the city seeks answers surrounding this high-profile incident.
TL;DR
- Shooting near Space Needle leaves two dead in Seattle.
- At least four people are reported injured.
- One person in custody; details remain unclear.
Tragedy Strikes Near Seattle’s Iconic Space Needle
On a somber evening in Seattle, gunfire erupted near the city’s landmark, the Space Needle, resulting in the deaths of two individuals and injuries to at least four others. The incident has cast a pall over the bustling area, which typically draws tourists and locals alike.
Ongoing Investigation Leaves Many Questions Unanswered
Authorities have confirmed that one suspect is currently being held in custody. However, details regarding the circumstances leading up to the shooting remain scarce. Law enforcement officials have yet to clarify the motives or confirm whether more suspects are being sought. As residents await further updates, an atmosphere of uncertainty persists throughout this corner of downtown Seattle.
The Scene: Shock and Disbelief at a Popular Landmark
The proximity of the violence to the Space Needle, one of the most recognized symbols of the Pacific Northwest, has heightened public concern. Witnesses described confusion and panic as shots rang out, with emergency responders rushing to assist victims. Several factors help explain why this event has gripped local attention:
- The high visibility and symbolic significance of the location
- The suddenness and severity of the attack during peak hours
- Anxieties about ongoing safety in public spaces
A Community Awaits Answers
As investigators work to piece together what happened, community leaders are urging calm and patience. The fact that at least four people were wounded—some critically—underscores both the seriousness of this attack and its impact on a city still reeling from previous incidents of violence. Meanwhile, many residents are seeking reassurance about security measures around prominent destinations such as the Seattle Center.
In summary, while one individual remains in custody, substantial gaps persist in our understanding of how events unfolded near this famous tower. For now, a shaken city waits for more information—and for any sign that clarity is on its way.

sources.news_title: Six Months In: Mixed Reviews for Seattle’s Mayor
sources.text:
With Mayor Katie Wilson’s honeymoon period over, Seattleites are grading her six-month performance as the city’s mayor. Opinions range from a few sour remarks to positive comments that credited Wilson working to chart a new pathway for the left.
There is no disputing Wilson began badly. She committed three initial rookie mistakes: bidding “bye” to departing businesses, hasty firing of a City Light superintendent, and strained relationships with the City Council.
Wilson reacted by shuffling her cabinet. She traded Chief of Staff Kate Brunette Kreuzer for Esther Handy, an experienced staffer. She put council relations fully under Deputy Mayor Brian Surratt and made changes to her communications staff. She replaced Seferiana Day as a mayoral spokesman with Sage Wilson, an experienced communicator, while drafting Dawn Schellenberg and Crystal Fincher to oversee office communications. In recent weeks, Wilson has moved on, leaving yet another opening.
Nevertheless, former council president Sara Nelson, speaking to KIRO radio host John Curley, recently ranked Wilson’s first six months as “unsatisfactory” and “below standard.” When asked about awarding the mayor a letter grade, Nelson, rumored as a possible future mayoral contender, conceded, “I’m not going there.”
For her part, the mayor was hesitant to grade her own performance in an interview with PubliCola’s Erica C. Barnett. Asked about her accomplishments, Wilson cited the city’s overwhelming passage of the Families, Education, Preschool and Promise (FEPP) levy. However, the mayor’s pledge to offer universal school lunches beginning this fall has been revised. Seattle Council President Joy Hollingworth and other councilmembers voted to delay starting the universal lunch program. Hollingworth, a long-time food bank volunteer, instead opted to provide vouchers to low-income families for weekend and holiday meals.
Meanwhile, the city’s World Cup games provided an unexpected opportunity for the new mayor to shine. She excelled in the unanticipated role of sports cheerleader, even heading out to play a pickup game of soccer on a West Seattle playing field with visiting Australians. In retrospect, Wilson wrote a celebratory op-ed about the city’s success “welcoming the world to Seattle.” She credited the work of the local organizing committee and others who worked long hours in preparation, resulting in “collective joy filling our street and public spaces.” She described the smooth operation as “what it looks like when government delivers.”
Despite pressures from activists opposed to surveillance cameras, the mayor had been persuaded to install cameras throughout the stadium district, turning them on just prior to the first World Cup games. Since conclusion of the Seattle games, Wilson left those cameras in place but turned off for now. Her decision is being attacked by both right and left factions. At the same time, the mayor, despite earlier promises, elected to permit hiring additional police and to retaining SPD Chief Shon Barnes.
While she had campaigned promising to set up 500 new shelter beds within a year, Wilson admittedly fell far short. In another campaign promise, Wilson had vowed to end sweeps of illegal encampments, but she did continue clearing of high-priority areas like sidewalks and parks. Critics said it sounded much like the policy of her predecessor, Bruce Harrell.
But unlike Mayor Harrell, a long-time councilmember, Wilson has experienced more difficulty when dealing with the City Council. For example, although her proposed doubling of the transit sales tax finally gained councilmembers’ approval, it first suffered through numbers of proposed amendments. The issue eventually will be decided by voters in the November election.
The more critical test of mayor-council relations lies ahead during this fall’s budget deliberations. The city is dealing with an anticipated $175 million budget shortfall that was not addressed during the Harrell years. Although city departments are already being asked to propose percentage reductions, expectations are that Mayor Wilson will be looking for new sources of revenue to balance the budget and fund future programs.
The mayor already has harmed a possible source of help. Perhaps taking a page out of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s successful left-wing slate, Wilson endorsed challengers to two powerful state legislators: Sen. Jamie Pedersen and Congressman Gerry Pollet. Wilson’s endorsements of opposition candidates Hannah Sabio-Howell, a community organizer, in the 43rd, and Ron Davis, a failed council candidate, in the 46th are bound to have consequences, even if neither is elected.
Wilson’s test of her political power in opposing the two effective long-time incumbents seems an exercise in political foolishness. While Mamdani, who also is a Democratic Socialist, won his mayoral race in New York City decisively, Wilson’s win was more narrow and less likely into translate into success.
In her Seattle Times’ opinion piece celebrating Seattle and its success participating in the World Cup games, Wilson expressed her enthusiasm for her adopted city, saying that it felt like “falling in love with Seattle once again.” Her optimistic conclusion: “Cities are where innovation happens and we all have an opportunity to write the next chapter.”

A witness account of the terrifying shooting, which took place near Seattle's Space Needle, revealed how scary the incident was.
It was reported on Sunday (July 26) that at least three people were killed, with four others left injured after gunfire broke out during a food festival in the area.
Families and attendees ran for cover as gunshots were heard, as witnesses recalled people falling over each other and baby strollers being left behind in the panic.
The shooting took place at around 6 PM local time during the annual Bite of Seattle festival, where thousands of people met at Seattle Center for the three-day event.
Police revealed that officers were already in the area when the first gunshots were heard at 6.01 PM, as they rushed towards the scene.
Authorities stated that two people died at the scene, while five others were initially treated by medics.
It was said that four victims, a two-year-old boy, a 23-year-old man and two adult women, were taken to hospital, where a third victim succumbed to their injuries.
Terrifying footage from the incident was shared online, revealing the chaos which ensued after gunshots were heard, as someone shouted "shooting" to warn others to take cover.
A witness named Paul Skinner spoke to the Seattle Times, admitting that he thought the gunfire was fireworks at first.
He recalled: “I just heard what sounded like what were some pretty loud fireworks at first,
“Then the energy changed. Mobs of people started flooding back down. I just told our staff to get down,” the 37-year-old said.
Estan Wakonabo, who was waiting for a photo booth with his girlfriend, said: “People were hiding, were pushing, people were falling on the ground, baby strollers were falling.
“Once I heard a ‘pop, pop, pop,’ that´s when I knew it was a shooter.”
He recalled that after getting his girlfriend to safety, he returned and found several victims lying on the ground.
Another witness, Kayla Carris, 22, recalled many rushing into the Seattle Armory, telling the publication: “Everyone was just throwing stuff and running.”
Adya Sengupta said that Seattle Fudge workers sheltered many terrified visitors, saying: “Inside the Seattle Armory was crazy, within seconds maybe 60-plus people had flooded the doors inside, all running towards that back corner with Seattle Fudge,” as reported by KING 5 News.
The FBI also responded to the scene, with a police investigation underway.
According to Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson, one person was detained in connection with the shooting, though it's believed that a second suspect fled.
Acting Police Chief Tyrone Davis made a shocking claim that the suspects were shooting at each other, though it is unclear what started the confrontation.
Authorities say that there is no ongoing threat to the public, as two weapons were recovered in the aftermath.
Mayor Wilson stated: “Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection and joy ended in gunfire.”
She also described the shooting as “an act of horrific violence.”
Wilson went on: “No one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event, gathering with friends or experiencing their city.”
King County Executive Girmay Zahilay also spoke out about the horrific event, admitting he was "horrified" by the incident.
“As someone who grew up in this community, I know what this event means to so many families, young people and neighbors across our region,” he said.
Zahilay added: “For years, the Bite has been one of Seattle’s signature summer traditions. To see violence at a place that brings so many people together is heartbreaking and unacceptable.”

A 27-year-old man has been shot at a demonstration on Capitol Hill, Washington, the Seattle Times has reported.
The disturbing incident occurred just as Seattle mayor Jenny Durkan and Police Chief Carmen Best were wrapping up a news conference regarding police brutality.
As they were concluding their talk, a gunman drove into the crowd and shot an unidentified 27-year-old man. The shooting occurred shortly before 8:30PM.
Coverage of the incident can be seen below:

The victim was transported to Harborview Medical Center, where he has been listed as being in a stable condition. The gunman was detained by police.
The unnamed gunman was dressed in blue jeans, a black sweatshirt, and a black baseball cap, shot the victim from inside his black car. He then exited the vehicle, gun in hand, and barged through demonstrators toward a line of police officers.
[[twitterwidget||https://twitter.com/YourAnonCentral/status/1269849013823500290]]
He was then detained and taken into custody.
Sunday night saw protesters gather near the intersection of Eleventh Avenue and Pine Street as people across the country - and the world - continue to call out the systemic injustices carried out against black people, not least seen by the recent deaths of George Floyd, Ahmaud Arbery, and Breonna Taylor.
[[twitterwidget||https://twitter.com/YourAnonCentral/status/1269850622913724416]]
As well as a call for justice, these ongoing protests are also demanding an end to police brutality and the racism that is so deeply entrenched in America and the western world.
The sudden arrival of the gunman's vehicle caused some demonstrators to shout, while others ran alongside it holding a metal panel in an effort to slow it down.
Witness B.J. Hayes was standing nearby when the car barreled down Eleventh Avenue from Pike Street toward hundreds of protesters. Hayes said:
"I thought he was plowing right into the crowd. I totally thought I was going to see a bunch of bodies flying through the air."
The male victim was shot as he appeared to reach into the driver's window. The Seattle Times reports that he fell backward as the driver exited the car.
Witness Matt McAlman, said he saw the victim raise his fist in the air when asked if he was going to be okay.
"It was empowering to see nothing is going to stop us," McAlman said.
After falling out of the vehicle, the victim was tended to by protesters, who applied a tourniquet to the man's arm. Volunteer medics then walked him to an ambulance.
[[twitterwidget||https://twitter.com/AGarlandPhoto/status/1269835122011865088]]
In a video recorded by Seattle journalist Alex Garland, the victim said: "I heard the gunshot go off in my arm. My whole thing was to protect those people down there."
The incident occurred as demonstrators faced off with police in the tenth night of protests. The protests had remained peaceful throughout the day.
However, tensions rose at around 10:20PM, as protesters continued to advance barriers set in place by law enforcement. "Whose streets? Our streets!" they shouted.
After warnings from officers, police resorted to using flash-bangs, pepper spray, and tear gas to disperse the remaining crowd.
Speaking during their video news conference earlier in the day, Mayor Jenny Durkan and Police Chief Carmen Best apologized for instances in which they said officers may have failed to deescalate tense moments, and resorted to using disproportionate force against demonstrators.
Durkan, who announced a 30-day ban on most use of tear gas Friday - only to see police deploy pepper-spray canisters and blast balls Saturday night, and again on Sunday - said:
"Use of force must be rare, it must be necessary and it must be proportional. Like everybody in our community, we know that was not the case, not only this week but in cases before.
"I know that safety was shattered for many by the images, sound and gas more fitting of a war zone, and for that, I’m sorry."
Durkan and Best then asked protesters to do more to help quell violence within the crowds, blaming "bad actors" for inciting clashes.

Three people were killed and eight others wounded early Sunday morning when gunfire erupted inside a Brooklyn hookah lounge and restaurant, multiple sources have reported, transforming what should have been a routine closing hour into a scene of chaos and tragedy.
Members of the New York City Office of the Chief Medical Examiner remove a man's body from Taste of the City Bar following the shooting. Credit: Kyle Mazza / Anadolu / Getty Images.According to NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch, officers received multiple emergency calls reporting shots fired inside the Taste of the City Lounge, located at 903 Franklin Avenue in Crown Heights, just before 3:30AM. Responding units found a devastating scene: three men (aged 27, 35, and one whose age has not yet been released) were pronounced dead at the location.
The victims, all patrons of the lounge, were caught in the crossfire of what police believe involved multiple gunmen. At least 36 shell casings were later recovered, pointing to a barrage of bullets fired in the tightly packed space.
Sources indicated that a dispute inside the crowded venue may have sparked the violence, though details remain under investigation, the New York Times reports.
The eight additional victims, five men and three women ranging in age up to 61, were rushed to nearby hospitals. Thankfully, police confirmed their injuries were non-life-threatening. Still, the sheer number of people harmed underscores the magnitude of the incident.
No arrests have yet been made, but law enforcement officials say they are searching for multiple suspects. Detectives also recovered a firearm in the area of Bedford Avenue and Eastern Parkway, though it is not yet confirmed whether that weapon was used in the shooting.
One witness, a 39-year-old man who declined to give his name, recalled the horrifying moment he saw a regular patron gunned down. “He’s a regular, he wasn’t doing nothing. Nothing to do with it … He’s just outside the bathroom, hitting a hookah, dead,” he told The New York Post, still shaken by the violence.
Credit: Kyle Mazza / Anadolu / Getty Images.The aftermath left investigators combing through a narrow, crowded lounge that workers described as just 12 feet wide but stretching far back, lined with tables, a bar, and little space to escape once the shooting began.
Officers in hazmat suits were later seen inside, gathering evidence near pools of blood and broken glass. Police also canvassed nearby businesses, including a Foodtown grocery store next door, seeking surveillance footage that might provide additional leads.
Commissioner Tisch acknowledged the tragedy but emphasized that shootings overall remain at historic lows in New York City.
“We have the lowest number of shooting incidents and shooting victims seven months into the year we’ve seen on record in the city of New York,” she said. “Something like this is, of course, thank God, an anomaly, and it’s a terrible thing that’s happened this morning.”
Credit: Kyle Mazza / Anadolu / Getty Images.Taste of the City Lounge, which opened in 2022 and advertises itself as offering American and Caribbean cuisine, hookah, DJs, and a full bar, was already known to authorities. The establishment was the scene of another shooting in November 2024, though that incident did not result in fatalities, according to The Guardian.
Police continue to appeal to the public for information. Anyone who witnessed the shooting or has relevant footage is urged to contact detectives as they work to piece together how a night out ended with such devastating loss of life.
Three people have been shot by a gunman who opened fire in New York's Times Square early Saturday morning.
The shooting erupted at around 1:20AM near the intersection of West 44th Street and 7th Avenue, right outside the Hard Rock Cafe, according to the NYPD, via the Guardian.
There has been a shooting in Times Square in New York City. Credit: Spencer Platt / GettyPolice say the gunfire broke out after a “verbal dispute between two people escalated,” with the teenage suspect allegedly pulling the trigger.
Three people were hurt in the incident — an 18-year-old woman grazed in the neck, a 19-year-old man shot in the right foot, and a 65-year-old man shot in the left leg, as reported by the New York Post.
All were rushed to Bellevue Hospital and are in stable condition.
Three people have been injured by the gunfire. Credit: Tim Drivas Photography / Getty“The perpetrator was engaged in a verbal dispute prior to the shooting with one of the victims,” an NYPD spokesperson told The Independent.
“He has been taken into custody and a firearm was also recovered. He has not been charged yet.” The teen’s identity has not been released due to his age.
Footage from the scene posted to social media shows crowds scattering in panic as police swarmed the area, surrounding a vehicle and directing bystanders away. One victim was filmed being wheeled into an ambulance on a stretcher.
The shooting comes during what NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch recently called the city’s lowest period of gun violence since records began.
Between January and July 2025, New York City recorded 412 shooting incidents — marking the tenth straight month of major crime decline.
Still, this latest outburst of violence is a stark reminder that the city is not immune to sudden, dangerous flare-ups.
Just last month, four people were killed in a mass shooting at an office building, including NYPD officer Didarul Islam, when a gunman targeted the NFL headquarters before dying of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Travis Kelce has offered his condolences following a horror shooting at the Kansas City Chiefs Super Bowl LVIII parade.
A tragedy unfolded on Wednesday (February 14) when a mass shooting occurred near Union Station in Kansas City, Missouri as Chiefs fans were leaving celebrations for the football team's recent success.
Despite the presence of more than 800 police officers, Kansas City Police Chief Stacey Graves revealed in a press conference that one victim was killed after gunshots rang out, with 22 victims sustaining injuries, as reported by PEOPLE.
Graves also disclosed that three people have been detained in connection to the incident and are under investigation, adding: "Right now we do not have a motive."
Paradegoer Arnold Sauther opened up about the harrowing shooting to ABC News, telling the publication that when the rally ended, the Chiefs went into Union Station, and fans followed the players to get autographs.
"Then, all of a sudden they all started running out, and you see all these policemen come running in there, and you knew something happened in the station," Sauther said.
One witness added that they hid near an elevator and "prayed," sharing: "There was yelling, and we didn't know if it was safe to leave, so we tried to block the doors. We heard the elevator start to move, so we opened the doors and ran out - there were officers there. I've never been so glad to see an officer in my life."
Among the injured, 11 children are being treated at Children's Mercy Kansas City, nine of them for gunshot wounds. All the children are expected to recover from their injuries, according to an update by the hospital's senior vice president Stephanie Meyer.
The children in their care are between the ages of six and 15. An adult who is a parent of one of the children is also being treated there, Meyer added.
"I'm angry at what happened today," the Kansas City Police Chief shared at the press conference. "The people who came to this celebration should expect a safe environment."
Kelce, who plays as a tight end for the American football team, took to X (formerly Twitter) to express his support to all those affected by the shooting in an emotional post.
"I am heartbroken over the tragedy that took place today. My heart is with all who came out to celebrate with us and have been affected. KC, you mean the world to me," the 34-year-old penned.
The Chiefs released a statement, penning: "We are truly saddened by the senseless act of violence that occurred outside of Union Station at the conclusion of today's parade and rally. Our hearts go out to the victims, their families, and all of Kansas City."
The NFL team added that "all of our players, coaches, staff and their families are safe and accounted for," while also sharing that they were in close contact with law enforcement officials and thanked first responders.
Chiefs' quarterback Patrick Mahomes also tweeted: "Praying for Kansas City," while his wife, Brittany Mahomes, addressed the tragedy on her Instagram Story: "Lives lost and people injured during something that was [supposed] to be a celebration. Horrible and traumatizing. So many prayers going to the families involved."
The shooting at the parade coincided with the sixth anniversary of the Parkland school massacre in Florida on February 14, 2018, which claimed the lives of 17 people.
President Joe Biden released a statement urging action on gun control, stating that for such an attack to occur during a Super Bowl parade "cuts deep in the American soul," as cited by The Guardian.
"Today's events should move us, shock us, shame us into acting. What are we waiting for? What else do we need to see? How many more families need to be torn apart?" he added.
The 81-year-old encouraged people to make their voices in Congress for efforts to prohibit assault weapons, limit high-capacity magazines, and strengthen background checks.
Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this tragedy.
A witness has described the terrifying moment a wounded victim fled a Manhattan office tower and cried for help after a gunman opened fire inside the building, killing four people, including an NYPD police officer, before turning the weapon on himself.
The shooting occurred on Monday evening at a Midtown skyscraper that houses major firms including Blackstone and the NFL. Authorities identified the shooter as 27-year-old Shane Tamura, who drove from Las Vegas and entered the building around 6PM, armed with an M4-style rifle.
Mass shooting in Manhattan leaves four dead, including NYPD officer. Credit: Anadolu / GettyAs Tamura entered the lobby, he immediately shot and killed NYPD officer Didarul Islam, 36, who was working a second job as a security guard and expecting his third child. He then opened fire on multiple people near the elevator bay before riding to the 33rd floor, where he fatally shot a tenant before dying from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Eyewitness Nekeisha Lewis was dining near the plaza outside when she heard a series of shots and saw a glass wall shatter. “I realized, ‘Oh my God, this is a shootout,’” she told NBC News. “It felt like a war zone.”
Moments later, Lewis said she saw a man run out of the building yelling: “Help, help, I’ve been shot!” She and her partner helped remove his backpack before fleeing to safety. “It’s the scariest situation I’ve ever been in,” she said. “I’ve cried three times since.”
Among the victims were Wesley LePatner, a senior executive at Blackstone and mother of two; Julia Hyman, 27, a property manager with Rudin; and Aland Etienne, a security guard praised by union leaders as a “New York hero.”
NYPD police office, Didarul Islam, lost his life in the attack. Credit: NYPD News X Account / Handout/Anadolu via Getty ImagesOne NFL employee, Craig Clementi, was reportedly struck by a ricocheting bullet while warning colleagues to evacuate. Despite his injury, Clementi stayed on the phone while being loaded into an ambulance to ensure others got to safety, according to a league source.
A handwritten suicide note found on Tamura suggested he targeted the NFL, which is headquartered in the building. In the letter, he claimed to suffer from chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a brain condition linked to football-related head trauma. He blamed the league for concealing the risks and referenced deceased NFL player Terry Long, writing: “Terry Long football gave me CTE and it caused me to drink a gallon of antifreeze.”
Police confirmed Tamura had a documented history of mental health issues. Investigators continue to examine the motive, including why he spared a woman he encountered in the elevator.
